Surah al-Tawbah (9), verse 1: "Acquittal from Allah and His Messenger" — the verse. The polytheists began to break the covenants between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Allah the Exalted commanded him to annul their covenants and throw them back at them, and He revealed this verse. The meaning: Allah and His Messenger are free of any obligation to give them covenants and to keep them, since they have broken them. Then He addressed the polytheists, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 2:

﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾ (sīrū fīhā āminīn ḥaythu shi'tum), i.e., travel in it secure wherever you wish. It means: from Shawwal until Safar. This is a respite granted by Allah, the Exalted, to the polytheists. So when this period has passed, they shall be killed wherever they are found. ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾ (lā tafutūnahu), that you cannot elude Him, even though you are granted this respite. ﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾ (muḫzī al-kāfirīn), humiliating them in this world through killing, and in the Hereafter through punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 3:

﴿And an announcement from Allah﴾ is a notification from Him ﴿and His Messenger to the people﴾, meaning: the Arabs ﴿on the day of the greater Hajj﴾. It is said: the day of Arafah. And it is said: the day of an-Nahr (the day of sacrifice). "The greater Hajj" is the Hajj with all its rites, and "the lesser" is the Umrah. ﴿That Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾. Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to inform the polytheists of the Arabs, on the day of the greater Hajj, of his disavowal of their covenants. So he sent ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), and when he recited to them the opening of Bara'ah (Surat at-Tawbah) on the day of an-Nahr, he then addressed the polytheists and said: ﴿So if you repent﴾, meaning you turn back from shirk, ﴿then it is better for you﴾ than persisting in it, ﴿but if you turn away﴾ from faith, ﴿then know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, meaning you will not escape Him through your own selves from punishment. Then He threatened them with the punishment of the Hereafter, saying: ﴿And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾. Then He excepted some people from the disavowal of covenants, saying:

﴿Except those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant, and who have not failed you in anything﴾ of the conditions of the covenant ﴿anything﴾, and they are the Banu Damra and the Banu Kinana. ﴿And have not supported anyone against you﴾, meaning they did not help any enemy against you. ﴿Then fulfil their covenant to them until their term ends﴾, meaning until the end of their term. Nine months of their term remained, so the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that it be fulfilled for them. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾, meaning those who fear Him through obedience to Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 5:

﴿Then when the sacred months have passed⦆ — that is, the period of respite. ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ — within the sacred precinct or outside it. ﴿And seize them﴾ — by taking them captive. ﴿And besiege them﴾ — if they take refuge in fortifications. ﴿And sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾ — on every route you might take. ﴿But if they repent﴾ — turn back from polytheism, ﴿and establish prayer﴾ — the obligatory prayer, ﴿and give zakat﴾ — from gold, silver, fruits and livestock. ﴿Then let them go their way﴾ — leave them alone and what they wish. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — toward whoever repents and believes.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 6:

﴿And if any one of the polytheists﴾ — those whom I commanded you to kill — ﴿seeks your protection﴾ — asks you for safe-conduct from being killed — ﴿then grant him protection﴾ — make him to be in safety — ﴿until he hears the words of Allah﴾ — the Qur'an — so that you may establish the proof of Allah against him and make the religion of Allah clear to him; ﴿then convey him to his place of safety﴾ — if he does not turn away from polytheism — so that he may consider his affair. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not know﴾ — they do all this because they are an ignorant people who do not know the religion of Allah and His oneness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 7:

﴿How can there be a covenant with God and His Messenger for the polytheists,﴾ while they harbor treachery and break their covenant? ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque,﴾ meaning: those whom He excepted from the disavowal. ﴿So long as they remain true to you, remain true to them.﴾ That is, as long as they keep to the fulfilment of their covenant, you too shall keep to yours.

How can they have a covenant with God and His Messenger? (Kayfa) means: how can they have their covenant, when their condition is that, if they gain the upper hand over you, they will not observe toward you any tie of kinship (illan) or any pact (dhimmah), but will please you with their mouths, saying with their tongues sweet words, while their hearts refuse to fulfil it. And most of them are defiant, treacherous, breakers of the covenant.

﴿They have exchanged the signs of Allah for a small price﴾: they replaced the Qur'an with the goods of this world. ﴿And they have averted [others] from His way﴾: they turned away from obeying Him. ﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾: wretched is what they used to do, namely their buying disbelief in exchange for faith.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 10:

﴿Lā yarqubūn﴾ (they do not observe): meaning these covenant-breakers. ﴿And it is those who are the transgressors﴾: those who exceed the lawful to the unlawful by breaking the covenant.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 11:

﴿If they repent﴾ from polytheism, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakat, then they are your brothers﴾ i.e., they are your brothers ﴿in religion. And We detail the verses﴾ We make clear the verses of the Qur'an ﴿for a people who know﴾ that they are from Allah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 12:

﴿And if they break their oaths﴾ means they violate their covenants, ﴿and attack your religion﴾ means they backbite you and disparage your religion, ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾ meaning the chiefs of misguidance, namely the champions of Quraysh. ﴿Indeed, they have no oaths﴾ meaning they have no covenants, ﴿so that perhaps they may desist﴾ meaning that they may cease from associating partners with Allah. Then he (al-Wahidi) urged the believers against them, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 13:

﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths﴾ meaning: the disbelievers of Makkah broke the covenant and aided Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah, ﴿and they resolved to expel the Messenger﴾ from Makkah, ﴿and they began the fight against you﴾ ﴿first time﴾ when they fought your allies Khuza'ah, so they began by breaking the covenant. ﴿Do you fear them?﴾ that some harm from fighting them might befall you, so that you abandon fighting them. ﴿Then God has more right that you fear Him﴾, so the harm of God's punishment has more right to be feared than abandoning their fight. ﴿If you are believers﴾, affirming God's punishment and His reward.

﴿Fight them; God will punish them at your hands﴾: He will kill them by your swords and spears. ﴿And disgrace them﴾: He will humiliate them through subjugation and capture. ﴿And heal the breasts of a believing people﴾: meaning the Banu Khuza'ah. Quraysh had aided the Banu Bakr against them, until they broke their covenant with them, so God healed their breasts from the Banu Bakr through the Prophet and the believers.

Here is the translation:

﴿And remove the rage of their hearts﴾ — its distress and grief — through the aid of Quraysh against them (bakran, i.e., a sudden attack). ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whomever He wills﴾ — from among the polytheists — such as Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Suhayl ibn Amr, whom Allah guided to Islam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 16:

﴿Or did you think﴾ O hypocrites, ﴿that you would be left﴾ in your present state of deception and concealment of hypocrisy? ﴿And Allah has not yet known those among you who strove﴾ with sincere intention, meaning: the knowledge that is connected to them after the struggle (jihad). This is because when fighting was prescribed, the hypocrite was distinguished from others, and the one who allies with the believers was distinguished from the one who allies with their enemies. ﴿And had not taken﴾ — that is, "And Allah has not yet known those who did not take" ﴿besides Allah and His Messenger and the believers as intimate friends (waliyjah)﴾, meaning: allies and intimates (dukhul).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 17:

﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾ It was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib when he was taunted with disbelief after being taken captive, and he said: "We maintain the Sacred Mosque, we guard the Ka'bah, and we give water to the pilgrims." So Allah rebuffed him with His saying: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾ by entering them and seeking refuge in them, because they are prevented from that. ﴿Bearing witness against themselves to disbelief﴾ by their prostrating to idols and taking them as gods. ﴿Those, their deeds have become worthless﴾ because their disbelief has nullified their reward.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, the ones who maintain the mosques of Allah﴾ by visiting them and sitting in them, ﴿are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish the prayer, and give the zakat﴾. The meaning is: whoever has this description is among the people who maintain the mosque. ﴿And do not fear﴾ in matters of religion ﴿except Allah. So it is expected that those﴾ — i.e., then those are the rightly guided ones, who hold fast to obedience to Allah that leads to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 19:

﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims﴾ The polytheists said: "The maintenance of the House of God and the attending to the watering are better than faith and jihad." So God the Exalted revealed this verse. The "providing of water for the pilgrims" means: giving them drink during the season (of pilgrimage). His words ﴿and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque﴾ mean: perfuming it and scenting it. ﴿Is (it) like one who believes﴾ i.e., like the faith of one who believes ﴿in God﴾? ﴿They are not equal in the sight of God﴾ in merit. ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ meaning: those who claimed that they were the people of maintenance; He called them wrongdoers because of their polytheism.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 20:

﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank with Allah﴾ than those who boasted of maintaining the House and providing water for the pilgrims. ﴿And those are the attainers of success﴾, those who attained their desire.
﴿Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him﴾ etc. That is: He informs them in this world of what awaits them in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 23:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾ etc. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to emigrate to Medina, there were some people whose wives, children and relatives clung to them, saying: "We implore you by Allah not to abandon us." He would then feel compassion for them and abandon the emigration. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾, meaning friends, whom you prefer to remain among, over the [believers in the] shade of the tree. ﴿If they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, meaning they choose it. ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then those are the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., they are polytheists like them.

When this verse was revealed, they said: "O Prophet of Allah, if we withdraw from those who oppose us in religion, we will be cut off from our fathers and our clans, our trade will cease, and our homes will be ruined." So Allah the Exalted revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 24:

﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, and the wealth you have acquired﴾ — i.e., that you have earned — ﴿and the trade you fear will decline, and the dwellings you are pleased with, are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His command.﴾ That is, remaining in Makkah. ﴿Until Allah brings His command﴾: the conquest of Makkah, whereupon the obligation of emigration (hijrah) will lapse. And this is a command of threat. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people.﴾ A threat to these people with the deprivation of guidance.

The Qur'an, 9:25 — Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz)

﴿Indeed, Allah has given you victory in many battlefields, and on the day of Hunayn﴾. Hunayn is a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought there against Hawazin and Thaqif. ﴿When your great number pleased you﴾. This was because they said: "We will not be defeated today for lack of numbers," and they were twelve thousand. ﴿But it availed you not﴾, meaning it did not repel anything from you. ﴿And the earth grew narrow for you despite its vastness﴾, meaning that because of the intensity of the fear that befell you, the earth, despite its breadth, became narrow for you, so that you could not find a place suitable for your standing. ﴿Then you turned back, fleeing﴾, meaning you were routed. Allah the Exalted informed them that they would not be overcome by their numbers, but would only be overcome by the victory of Allah.

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility (sakinah)﴾, which is that by which the heart is settled, from the gentleness and mercy of Allah, ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see﴾. He means: the angels. ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾ by your swords and your spears. ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 27:

﴿Then Allah relents after that toward whom He wills﴾ — that is, He guides them to Islam from among the disbelievers. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — toward those who believe.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 28:

﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are impure﴾ (they do not perform ghusl from janabah (ritual impurity from sexual intercourse or emission of semen) nor perform wudu' (ablution) from hadath (minor ritual impurity)), ﴿so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ (i.e., let them not enter the Haram). They were prevented from entering the Haram, for the Haram is forbidden to the polytheists. ﴿After this, their year﴾ (meaning: the year of the Conquest). When they were prevented from entering the Haram, the Muslims said: "They used to bring provisions, so now the trade will be cut off from us." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾ (faqr), ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾. So the people of Jeddah, San'a' and Jurash embraced Islam and brought food to Makkah, and Allah sufficed them against what they had feared. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing﴾ of what sets you right, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has ordained concerning the polytheists. Then, concerning the fighting against the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, He revealed His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 29:

﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day﴾ meaning: their faith is not like the faith of those who affirm the oneness (of Allah) (muwahhidun), and their faith is not (true) faith if they do not believe in Muhammad. ﴿And who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾ meaning: wine and gambling (maysir). ﴿And do not adopt the religion of truth﴾ meaning: they do not practise the religion of Islam. ﴿Until they give the jizyah﴾ and it is what the covenanted (mu'ahad) pays in return for his covenant. ﴿With willing submission (ʿan yadin)﴾ they give it with their own hands, walking with it unwillingly, and they do not come with it riding, nor send it (by others). ﴿And they are humbled (wa-hum saghirun)﴾ abased and subdued; they are dragged to the place where it is collected from them, and forcibly seized until they hand it over from their own hand.

The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their saying from their mouths. (Qur'an 9:30)

It has no proof and no clear evidence; it is merely a saying from the mouth alone. ﴿Yuḍāhi'ūn﴾ (they imitate) — they resemble the saying of the polytheists when they said, "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Allah has informed about them in His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Him sons and daughters﴾ (Qur'an 6:100).

﴿Qātalahumu Allāh﴾ (May Allah destroy them) — may Allah curse them.

﴿Annā yu'fakūn﴾ (How are they turned away?) — how are they turned away from the truth after the evidence has become clear, so that they make for Allah a son? This is an expression of wonder directed at the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 31:

﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks﴾ — their scholars and their worshippers — ﴿as lords﴾ — gods — ﴿besides Allah﴾, in that they obeyed them in declaring lawful what Allah had made unlawful and declaring unlawful what Allah had made lawful. ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary﴾ — they took him as a lord. ﴿And they were not commanded﴾ in the Torah and the Gospel ﴿except to worship one God﴾ — the One besides whom there is no god. ﴿Glory be to Him above what they associate﴾ — exalting Him above their polytheism.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 32:

﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾ — they want to quench the religion of Islam by their denial. ﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light﴾ — except that He will make His religion prevail.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 33:

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger﴾ Muhammad, ﴿with guidance﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿and the religion of truth﴾, that is, the ḥanīfiyya (the pure monotheistic faith of Abraham), ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, that is, that He may make it high above all the other religions.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 34:

﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis (ahbar) and the monks (ruhban)﴾ from among the jurists (fuqaha') and scholars (ulama') of the People of the Book ﴿do consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾, meaning: what they take as bribes (rushan) in judgment ﴿and avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾, and turn people away from faith in Muhammad, peace be upon him. Then He revealed, concerning those who withhold zakat from among the People of the Qiblah: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah﴾, who do not pay its zakat ﴿- give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾, informing them that there is for them a painful punishment.

﴿On the Day it will be heated﴾ on the Day their treasures are put into the Fire until it is heated and its heat intensifies, ﴿and their foreheads, sides and backs will be branded with it﴾ meaning: they will be stuck to their foreheads, their sides and their backs, until the heat reaches their insides. And it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, and you withheld it from the right of God. ﴿So taste﴾ the punishment for ﴿what you used to hoard﴾."

The number of months with Allah is twelve months. The number of the Muslims' months, which they are commanded to make the count of their year: twelve months, according to the phases of the moon and the sighting of the crescents, not as the people of Rome and Persia count it. ﴿In the Book of Allah﴾ in the Preserved Record (al-Imam) that is with Allah, which He wrote on the day He created the heavens and the earth. ﴿Of them, four are sacred﴾: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram; the violation of what is forbidden in them is magnified more severely than in other months. ﴿That is the upright religion﴾: the straight reckoning. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾: guard yourselves against yourselves during the sacred months, for good deeds are multiplied in them, and likewise bad deeds. ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together, as they fight against you all together﴾: fight them all, and do not show leniency by abandoning fighting, since they permit fighting all of you. ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾: with His friends who fear Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 37:

﴿Indeed, the nasi' (postponement)﴾ is the postponement of the sanctity of a month that God had made sacred to another month that He had not made sacred. This is because the Arabs in the pre-Islamic period would sometimes make lawful the sacred month and make sacred in its place Safar. So God, exalted is He, informed that all of this is ﴿an increase in disbelief﴾, since they made lawful what God had made unlawful and made unlawful what God had made lawful. ﴿Through it, those who disbelieve are led astray﴾ by that postponement, ﴿they make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year﴾. When they fought in it, they made it lawful and made Safar sacred in its place; and when they did not fight in it, they made it sacred. ﴿So that they may conform⁠﴾ to ﴿the number of what God has made sacred﴾, meaning: they did not make lawful a month of the sacred months except that they made sacred in its place a month of the lawful months, and they did not make sacred a month of the lawful months except that they made lawful in its place a month of the sacred months, so that the sacred months would not exceed the four that God had made sacred, and thus there would be conformity in number. ﴿The evil of their deeds was made attractive to them﴾: Satan made that attractive to them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 38:

﴿O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you﴾ It was revealed to urge the believers to join the expedition to Tabuk, because they were called to it at a time of hardship for the people, drought in the land, and intense heat. Going out was difficult for them, so God Most High revealed: ﴿What is [wrong] with you, that when it is said to you, "Go forth in the way of God," you grow heavy toward the earth?﴾ That is, go out for jihad to fight the enemy. ﴿You grow heavy toward the earth﴾ means you love to remain [at home]. ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world instead of the Hereafter?﴾ That is, instead of the Hereafter, meaning Paradise. ﴿Then the enjoyment of the life of this world, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but little﴾ He means: the entire world, ﴿but little﴾ compared with something of Paradise.

﴿Unless you go forth﴾, that is, go out with your Prophet to jihad, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾, with drought and the withholding of rain, ﴿and will replace you with another people﴾, that is, He will bring other people by whom He supports His Messenger, ﴿and you will not harm Him at all﴾, because God protected him from people, and He does not forsake him, even if you are sluggish. Just as the scarcity of his helpers did not harm him when he was in Makkah and the disbelievers plotted against him, so God took up his support, and that is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 40:

﴿If you do not support him, [know that] Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved drove him out, the second of two.﴾ That is: they compelled him to leave when they plotted to kill him, so they were the cause of his departure from Makkah as a fugitive from them. ﴿The second of two⦆ That is, one of two, he (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه). The meaning is: Allah supported him when he was alone, except for Abu Bakr. ﴿When they were both in the cave⦆ It is a cave in a mountain of Makkah called Thawr. ﴿When he said to his companion⦆ Abu Bakr: ﴿Do not grieve⦆ This was because he feared for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the pursuit, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us⦆, He will prevent them from us and support us. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility⦆ He cast into the heart of Abu Bakr that by which he became calm. ﴿And supported him⦆ That is, His Messenger, ﴿with hosts you did not see⦆ He strengthened him and aided him with angels on the day of Badr. He informed that He turned away from him the plotting of his enemies, then made him prevail: He supported him with angels on the day of Badr. ﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest⦆, and it is the word of polytheism. ﴿And the word of Allah is the highest⦆, meaning: the word of monotheism, because it rose high and prevailed, and this was on the day of Badr.

﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ (young and old), ﴿and strive with your wealth and your persons in the way of Allah. That is better for you﴾ than dragging yourselves to the earth (i.e., than sluggishness), ﴿if you only knew﴾ what reward and recompense you have. Then it was revealed concerning the hypocrites who stayed behind from this expedition:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 42:

﴿Had it been a near gain﴾, i.e., had what they were called to been a near spoil of war (ghanima) ﴿and a moderate journey﴾, near and easy ﴿they would have followed you﴾, out of greed for the spoil ﴿but the distance seemed long to them﴾, the journey ﴿And they will swear by God﴾ before you when you return to them ﴿"Had we been able, we would have gone out with you"﴾, had we been capable and had we had ample wealth ﴿They destroy themselves﴾ through lying and hypocrisy ﴿And God knows that they are liars﴾, for they were able to go out.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 43:

﴿Almighty God pardon you. Why did you grant them permission?﴾ The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had granted permission to a group to stay behind from him without consultation, and it was not for him to carry out anything except by revelation. So God, glory be to Him, rebuked him and said: why did you grant them permission to stay behind? ﴿Until it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars﴾, until you knew who among them had a valid excuse and who had no excuse, so that your permission would be for the one who had an excuse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 44:

﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission﴾ to sit back and stay behind from jihad, out of reluctance ﴿to strive﴾ in the way of Allah ﴿with their wealth and their lives﴾ — the verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 45:

﴿Only those ask your permission﴾ to stay behind, ﴿who do not believe in God and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt﴾, they doubted their religion, ﴿so they are wavering in their doubt﴾, they persist in their uncertainty.

"Had they truly intended to go out, they would have made ready for it some preparation" [from the provisions and mounts, because they were well-off]. "But Allah disliked their setting out" [He did not want their going out with you], "so He held them back" [He forsook them and made them sluggish], "and it was said, 'Sit with those who sit'" [a revelation cast into their hearts; meaning, Allah inspired them with the causes of abandonment], "[sit] with those who sit" [the disabled and those with harm]. Then He explained why He disliked their going out, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 47:

﴿If they had gone out among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption.﴾ He says: If they had gone out, they would have corrupted your affair for you. ﴿And they would have hastened between your ranks﴾ — they would have hurried to spread tale-bearing (al-namimah) in order to sow discord among you. ﴿Seeking to cause you fitnah﴾ — they would discourage you and scatter your word, until you quarrel and are thrown into fitnah. ﴿And among you are those who listen to them﴾ — those who hear their words and obey them; and if these hypocrites had accompanied them, they would have corrupted them for you. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ — the hypocrites.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 48:

﴿Indeed, they had sought discord before [this], and they had plotted against you the affairs [i.e., they schemed] until the truth came and the decree of Allah was manifest while they were averse.﴾

Note on the text: the translation above is the Qur'anic quotation rendered as it stands in the passage; the commentary itself follows.

Al-Wahidi: They sought evil and harm for you before Tabuk, namely that a group of them intended to assassinate him on the night of al-Aqabah. ﴿And they plotted against you the affairs﴾ they strove in devising stratagems against you and in scheming against you. ﴿Until the truth came﴾ — the verse continues — meaning: until Allah disgraced them by making the truth manifest and strengthening the religion, though they were averse to it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 49:

﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial."﴾ It was revealed concerning Jadd ibn Qays, the hypocrite. He said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Would you be interested in fighting the Banu al-Asfar (the Byzantines)? You could take from them concubines and attendants." He said: "Grant me leave, O Messenger of Allah, to stay behind from you, and I will help you with my wealth." ﴿And do not put me to trial﴾ with the daughters of the Banu al-Asfar, for I am infatuated with women, and I fear that if I see them I will not be able to refrain from them. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Verily, into trial they have already fallen.﴾ That is: they fell into polytheism through their hypocrisy, and they stayed behind from your command. ﴿And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers.﴾ That is, it surrounds those who disbelieve and gathers them together.

﴿If good befalls you﴾, namely victory and booty, ﴿it distresses them; and if a misfortune strikes you﴾, namely killing and defeat, ﴿they say, "We had already taken our precaution"﴾, meaning: we had already taken our precaution and acted with prudence when we held back, ﴿and they turn away﴾, meaning: they go away, ﴿rejoicing﴾, meaning: pleased with themselves for that and for the harm that has befallen you.

Say, "Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed and written for us. He is our Protector (mawlana), our Helper. So let the believers put their trust in Allah." That is, let the believers entrust their affairs to Him, being content with His arrangement.

**Al-Wahidi's commentary (al-Wajiz) on Surah 9, verse 52:**

﴿Say, "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best outcomes?"﴾ That is, do you wait for anything to befall us except (the) *ghanima* (spoils of war) or *shahada* (martyrdom)? ﴿And we await for you﴾ we wait ﴿that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself﴾ with a calamity from the sky, ﴿or by our hands﴾ that He will permit us to kill you, so we kill you. ﴿So wait; indeed we are waiting with you.﴾ That is, await the promises of Satan; indeed we await the promises of God, namely the manifestation of His religion and the destruction of those who oppose it.

Then, in the second and third verses, He mentions that what they spent in jihad will not be accepted from them, because among them were those who said to the Messenger of God ﷺ, "Stay behind, and I will help you with my wealth." God informed that He does not accept that, whether they did it willingly or unwillingly. He made clear that what prevents the acceptance of this is their disbelief in God and His Messenger, their laziness in the prayer, because they do not hope for reward from it, and their reluctance to spend in the way of God, because they regard it as a loss.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 55:

﴿So do not let their wealth or their children impress you.﴾ Do not admire what We have bestowed upon them of abundant wealth and children. ﴿Indeed, Allah intends only to punish them thereby in this worldly life﴾ meaning: through the calamities in them. So they are a punishment for them, while for the believer it is a reward. ﴿And that their souls depart﴾ and their spirits leave them ﴿while they are disbelievers﴾ upon disbelief.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 56:

﴿And they swear by Allah that they are indeed of you﴾ i.e., they are believers, and they are not believers. ﴿But they are a people who are afraid﴾ they fear, so they swear out of dissimulation (taqiyyah) toward you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 57:

﴿Had they found a refuge﴾ (malja'): a place of escape, ﴿or caves﴾ (maghaarat): underground passages, ﴿or a place of entry﴾ (mudkhal): a way they could enter, ﴿they would turn towards it﴾: they would return to it, ﴿and they would rush off headlong﴾ (yajmahoon): they would hurry with a speed that nothing could turn their faces back from. That is: if it were possible for them to flee from among the Muslims by any means whatsoever, they would have fled and not remained among them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 58:

﴿And among them﴾ — that is, among the hypocrites — ﴿are those who find fault with you﴾, reproaching you and criticising you ﴿concerning﴾ the matter of ﴿the alms (sadaqat)﴾. They say: "Muhammad only gives them to whomever he likes. If you give them a great deal, they are pleased; and if you give them a little, they become angry." Then, in the second verse, he mentioned that if they were content with that and put their trust in God, it would be better for them, and this is His saying:

﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them, and said, "Allah is sufficient for us; Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger; indeed, we turn to Allah in hope."﴾ Then He explained to whom the ṣadaqāt (obligatory charities) are due, saying:

Verse 9:60 — "Indeed, the alms are only for the poor (al-fuqara') and the needy (al-masakin) and those employed to collect them (al-'amilina 'alayha) and those whose hearts are to be reconciled (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum) and for freeing captives (fi al-riqab) and for those in debt (al-gharimin) and for the cause of Allah (fi sabil Allah) and for the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), an obligation from Allah."

Al-Wahidi's commentary (al-Wajiz):

﴿Indeed, the alms are for the poor﴾ — they are those who abstain from asking. ﴿And the needy﴾ — those who ask and go about among the people. ﴿And those employed to collect them﴾ — the collectors who gather the alms (sadaqah). ﴿And those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾ — they were a group of the nobles of the Arabs whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) won over so that they would turn their people away from him and help him against his enemy. ﴿And for freeing captives﴾ — the mukatabun (slaves who have contracted to purchase their freedom). ﴿And for those in debt﴾ — the people of debt. ﴿And for the cause of Allah﴾ — the warriors and those stationed at the frontier (al-murabitun). ﴿And for the wayfarer﴾ — one who is cut off on his journey. ﴿An obligation from Allah﴾ — which Allah has enjoined upon the wealthy in their wealth.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 61:

﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet﴾ by transmitting his words and finding fault with him, ﴿and they say, "He is an ear."﴾ They said among themselves: "We say whatever we wish, then we come to him and swear to him, and he believes us, because he is an ear." An ear (udhun) is one who listens to everything that is said to him. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "An ear of good for you"﴾, meaning: a listener to what is good and righteous, not a listener to evil and corruption. Then He emphasized and clarified this, saying: ﴿He believes in Allah﴾, meaning: he listens to what Allah sends down to him and so believes in it, ﴿and believes the believers﴾, and trusts the believers in what they report to him, not the disbelievers, ﴿and is a mercy for those of you who believe﴾, meaning: he is a mercy, because he was the cause of their faith.

﴿They swear to you by Allah, to please you.﴾ These hypocrites swear, regarding what has reached you about them concerning their harm to the Messenger and their reviling of him, that they did not do that, and they swear to please you with their oath. ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him.﴾ So that they believe in both of them and affirm them, if they are truly upon what they display.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 64:

﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah will be sent down upon them﴾ upon the believers, ﴿informing them﴾ ﴿of what is in their hearts﴾ of envy toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers. That is because they were afraid of being exposed and disgraced. ﴿Say: Mock, [as you wish]﴾ an imperative of threat. ﴿Indeed, Allah will bring out﴾ make manifest ﴿what you fear﴾ its becoming manifest.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 65:

﴿And if you ask them﴾ about what they were engaged in of mockery, ﴿they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing."﴾ This was because a man among the hypocrites said during the expedition of Tabuk: "I have never seen the likes of these people: greediest of stomachs, most lying of tongues, and most cowardly at the time of meeting," meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of this, so this speaker came to make an excuse, but found that the Qur'an had preceded him. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were only conversing, playing, and talking about the talk of the riders, by which we cut off the road for ourselves." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿We were only conversing﴾, i.e., in vain talk, as the riders converse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: ﴿Was it at Allah and His signs and His Messenger that you were mocking?﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 66:

﴿Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief.﴾ That is: your disbelief has become apparent after you displayed belief. ﴿If We pardon one faction among you, We will punish another faction﴾ And this is because they were three men: two of them mocked and one laughed, and he was the one who was pardoned. When this verse was revealed, he was freed from hypocrisy.

The Hypocrites, men and women, are of one another: they share the same religion. ﴿They enjoin what is evil﴾, that is, disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And forbid what is good﴾, that is, following him. ﴿And they withhold their hands﴾, that is, from spending in the way of Allah. ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾: they abandoned the command of Allah, so He abandoned them from every good and forsook them. ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾, those who go outside what Allah has commanded.
﴿Allah has promised the hypocrites﴾ — the verse is clear. Then He addressed them, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 69:

﴿Like those before you﴾ meaning: you have acted like the deeds of those before you. ﴿So they enjoyed their share (khalaq) [of worldly pleasure]﴾ they were content with their portion of the world, and so you too did the same as they did. ﴿And you engaged in idle talk (khudtum)﴾ in slandering the Prophet ﷺ, just as they engaged in slandering their prophets. ﴿Those, their deeds have become worthless (habitat) in this world and the Hereafter﴾ because they will not be accepted from them, nor will they be rewarded for them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 70:

﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them﴾ Has there not come to them the report of those who were destroyed in the world for their sins, so that they might take warning? Then he named them: ﴿the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Abraham﴾ meaning Nimrod, ﴿and the companions of Madyan﴾ the people of Shuʿayb, ﴿and the overturned cities﴾ and the companions of the overturned cities, which were the villages of the people of Lot. ﴿Allah would not have wronged them﴾ meaning, would not have punished them before the sending of the Messenger. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ by denying the messengers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 71:

﴿And the believing men and the believing women are allies of one another﴾ in mercy and love; ﴿they enjoin what is right﴾ they call to Islam; ﴿and forbid what is wrong﴾ polytheism (shirk) with Allah; the verse...

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 72:

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence.﴾ He means palaces of zabarjad (chrysolite), pearls, and rubies. ﴿In gardens of Eden.﴾ It is the capital (qaṣabah) of Paradise, and its ceiling is the Throne of the Most Merciful. ﴿And approval from Allah is greater.﴾ Greater than what is described.

Translation:

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾ with the sword, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾ with the tongue and argument, ﴿and be harsh upon them﴾, meaning: be severe in rebuke and look at them with hatred and detestation.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 74:

﴿They swear by Allah that they did not say [it]﴾. It was revealed when the hypocrites spoke evil of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), slandered the religion, and said: "If we return to Medina, we will set a crown upon the head of Abdullah ibn Ubayy, by which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will be made to look inferior." This was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he summoned them, and they swore that they had not said it. ﴿And they had already uttered the word of disbelief﴾: the Messenger (ﷺ) reproached them and they had slandered the religion. ﴿And they resolved upon what they could not attain﴾: from their setting a crown upon the head of Ibn Ubayy. It is also said: it refers to their plot to assassinate the Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿And they did not resent﴾, that is, they disliked, ﴿except that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty﴾ through the spoils of war, until wealth came to them. That is: they acted contrary to what was required, for instead of being thankful for their wealth, they resented it. Then He offered them repentance, saying: ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away﴾, that is, turn away from faith, ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world﴾ by killing, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ with the Fire. ﴿And they will have no protector or helper on earth﴾: no one among the Muslims will take them as an ally.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 75:

﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God﴾ meaning: Tha'labah ibn Hatib made a covenant with his Lord that if He made him prosperous, he would give to every person with a right his due. God did so, but he did not fulfill what he had covenanted and withheld the zakat. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity﴾, that is, we will certainly give sadaqah (voluntary charity) ﴿and we will surely be among the righteous﴾, that is, we will surely do what the people of righteousness do with their wealth.

Then He caused them to follow it with hypocrisy (﴿فأعقبهم نفاقاً﴾): He made the outcome of their affair to be that, by depriving them of repentance, so that they died upon hypocrisy, as a recompense for their breaking of the promise and their lying in the covenant. This is His saying: ﴿until the Day they meet Him﴾, and the verse [continues].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 79:

﴿Those who find fault with﴾ (yalmizuna) means: they blame and backbite ﴿the volunteers﴾ (al-mutawwi'in), i.e., those who give voluntary (nafl) charity, ﴿among the believers, concerning the charities﴾. The reason for its revelation: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged charity, so some of the Companions brought large amounts of wealth, and others, who were the poor, brought little. The hypocrites backbited them and said: "Whoever gave more did so for show, and whoever gave less wanted to make himself mentioned." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿and those who find nothing but their effort﴾, which is the little with which they make their living, ﴿so they mock them, Allah mocks them﴾, meaning He repaid them for their mockery when they arrived in the Fire. Then Allah made the Messenger despair of their faith and forgiveness, so he said:

"Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them" (Q. 9:80). This is an option (takhyir) given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then He said: "Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times" (Q. 9:80), meaning: even if you increase the supplication for forgiveness for the hypocrites (munafiqin), Allah will not forgive them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 81:

﴿Those who stayed behind rejoiced﴾, meaning: the hypocrites who lagged behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿in their sitting [at home]﴾, by their staying behind, ﴿in opposition to the Messenger of Allah﴾, acting in opposition to him, ﴿and said, "Do not go forth in the heat." Say, "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat,"﴾ — if only they understood — meaning, if only they knew that their destination is to it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 82:

﴿Let them laugh a little﴾ in the world, because it will cut off from them; ﴿and let them weep much﴾ in the Fire, a weeping that will never cease; ﴿as a recompense for what they used to earn﴾ in the world of hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 83:

﴿Then if Allah brings you back﴾ returns you ﴿to a group of them﴾, meaning: those who stayed behind in Medina, ﴿and they ask your permission to go out﴾ to fight alongside you, ﴿then say: "You shall never go out with me, ever, and you shall never fight an enemy with me"﴾ from among the People of the Book, ﴿You were content with sitting at home the first time﴾ when you did not go out to Tabuk, ﴿so sit with those who stay behind﴾, meaning: the women, the children and the chronically ill who remain behind those who go off on journeys. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was forbidden from praying over them when they died and from supplicating for them when standing at their graves, so he said:

The passage is a short commentary note on Qur'an 9:85.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 85:

﴿And do not let their wealth impress you﴾ Its explanation has already passed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 86:

﴿And when a surah is sent down, [commanding]: "Believe in Allah and strive alongside His Messenger," those of wealth among them ask your permission [to stay behind].﴾ That is: the people of wealth and ability ask you for permission to remain behind (al-takhallluf) [from the campaign].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 87:

﴿They are content to be with the women who remain behind (al-khawalif)﴾ the women who are left behind in the house, ﴿and a seal has been set upon their hearts﴾ by hypocrisy, ﴿so they do not understand﴾ they do not comprehend faith, its laws, and the command of Allah.

﴿And those who make excuses among the Bedouins came﴾: the *mu'adhdhirun* are those who offer excuses. They were a people ﴿from among the Bedouins (al-A'rab)﴾ who made excuses to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for staying behind, so he granted them their excuse. This is His saying ﴿that permission may be given to them﴾, meaning to remain behind. ﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat [at home]﴾: they did not believe His Prophet, and they made their Islam a shield (*junnah*). Then he mentioned the people who had a valid excuse, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 91:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak﴾ meaning: the chronically ill, the elderly, and the infirm, ﴿nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, [there is] no blame if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ they make their deeds pure of deceit toward them both. ﴿There is no path [of blame] against the good-doers﴾ meaning no way of punishment, because their way has been closed by their goodness. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward whoever is characterized by these qualities.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 92:

﴿Nor [is there blame] upon those who came to you that you might provide them with mounts,﴾ It was revealed concerning seven men who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to carry them upon animals. He said, ﴿I cannot find anything to carry you on,﴾ so they turned back weeping, out of longing for jihad and grief at their lack of means.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 94:

﴿They will make excuses to you﴾ with falsehoods ﴿when you return to them﴾ from this expedition. ﴿Say: "Do not make excuses; we will never believe you﴾ we will never accept you as truthful. ﴿God has informed us of your news﴾ God has informed us of your inner secrets and what your breasts conceal. ﴿And God will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger﴾ regarding whether you will repent from hypocrisy when you ask forgiveness, or persist in it. ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ to the One who knows what is hidden from us of your consciences ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ that is, He will inform you of what you used to conceal and reveal.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 95:

﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them﴾ — when you return to them from Tabuk — that they were not able to go out. ﴿That you may leave them alone﴾ — leaving with forgiveness. ﴿So leave them alone﴾ — abandon their speech and their greetings. ﴿Indeed, they are impure (rijs)﴾ — their deeds are foul, from the deeds of Satan. Then it was revealed concerning the Banu Asad and Ghatafan:

The Bedouins are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy ﴿الأعراب أشدُّ كفراً ونفاقاً﴾ than the people of the settled towns (من أهل المدر), because they are more uncouth and harsher (لأنَّهم أجفى وأقسى). ﴿وأجدر﴾ meaning more fitting, more deserving and more entitled ﴿أن لا يعلموا حدود ما أنزل الله﴾ not to know the limits of what God has sent down, namely the lawful and the unlawful.

[Qur'an 9:98] "And among the Bedouins is he who takes what he spends as a fine (ghar­am)" — because he does not hope for any reward for it. "And he awaits misfortunes for you" — and he waits for the affair to turn against you through the death of the Messenger, peace be upon him. "Upon them is the misfortune of evil" — upon them turns calamity and disgrace, so they see in Muhammad and his religion only what displeases them. Then it was revealed concerning those among them who embraced Islam:

ﷺ

﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and take what they spend as means of nearness to Allah﴾, seeking nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by it, ﴿and the prayers of the Messenger﴾, meaning: his supplication for them with good and blessing. The meaning is that he seeks nearness to Allah through his charity and the supplication of the Messenger. ﴿Unquestionably, it is indeed a means of nearness for them﴾, meaning: a light and an honour in the sight of Allah.

"And the foremost, the first [to embrace Islam] among the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers)" — i.e., those who bore witness at Badr, and those among them who believed before the arrival of the Messenger ﷺ upon them; these are the foremost of both groups. It is also said: he intended everyone among his Companions whom he encountered, for they all preceded this Ummah by their companionship with the Prophet ﷺ and by seeing him. "And those who followed them with excellence" — i.e., whoever follows them in their ways until the Day of Resurrection, from among those who speak well of them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 101:

﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾ meaning: Muzayna, Juhayna and Ghifar. ﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾ the Aws and the Khazraj. ﴿They have persisted in hypocrisy﴾ they clung to it and refused anything other than it. ﴿We will punish them twice﴾ with sicknesses and calamities in this world, and with the punishment of the grave. ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾ which is abiding eternally in the Fire.

And others have acknowledged their sins, [having failed to join the expedition], [they] mixed a righteous deed [which was their struggle with the Prophet ﷺ before this] with another wrong deed [their lagging behind from this expedition]. "Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance" — "perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is a binding certainty — "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." Then He accepted the repentance of these people and excused them. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are our wealth that kept us back from you; take it from us as charity, purify us, and ask forgiveness for us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have not been commanded to take anything from your wealth," so Allah the Exalted revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 103:

﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a third of their wealth, and it was an expiation (kaffarah) for the sins they had committed. This is His saying: ﴿that you may purify them﴾, meaning: this charity purifies them from sins. ﴿And cleanse them thereby﴾, i.e., you, O Muhammad, raise them through this charity from the station of the hypocrites. ﴿And pray upon them﴾, i.e., supplicate for them. ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, i.e., your supplications are something their souls find comfort in, [knowing] that Allah has accepted their repentance. ﴿And Allah is Hearing﴾ of their words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of their remorse.

When the repentance of these men was revealed, those who had not repented among those who had stayed behind said: "These men were with us yesterday; they were not spoken to and not sat with. What is their situation?" That was because when the Prophet (ﷺ) returned to Madinah, he forbade the believers from speaking with the hypocrites and sitting with them. So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 104:

﴿Did they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charitable gifts?﴾ He accepts them. ﴿And that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Most Merciful.﴾ He turns with mercy and forgiveness toward whoever turns back to Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 105:

﴿And say: Work,﴾ O assembly of My servants, the good-doer and the wrongdoer, ﴿for Allah will see your deed, and His Messenger, and the believers.﴾ That is: Allah will make them aware of what is in the hearts of their brethren of good and evil, so they will love the good-doer and hate the wrongdoer, by Allah placing that in their hearts. The remainder of the verse has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 106:

﴿And others are deferred for the command of Allah﴾: postponed until Allah decides concerning them what He decides. They were Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Murarah ibn al-Rabi'. They had stayed behind without an excuse, and then they did not go to great lengths in apologizing as those did who gave their wealth in charity. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) suspended their matter, and they were shunned, until there was revealed His saying: ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾ and the verses that follow. ﴿Either He will punish them﴾ with His punishment, as a recompense for them, ﴿or He will turn to them [in forgiveness]﴾ by His grace. ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of what their state will come to, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He does with them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 107:

﴿And those who took⁠﴾ — and among them are those who took a mosque, and they were twelve men from the hypocrites (munafiqun). They built a mosque by which they harmed the mosque of Quba', and this is His saying: ﴿harm and disbelief﴾ — disbelief in the Prophet (ﷺ) and in what he brought. ﴿And division among the believers﴾ — by it they divided their community, for they used to pray together in the mosque of Quba', so they built the mosque of harm so that some of them would pray in it, and they would thereby differ among themselves because of that. ﴿And in preparation﴾ — and in waiting ﴿for one who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾, meaning Abu 'Amir al-Rahib, who had gone out to Syria to bring an army with which to fight the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he sent to the hypocrites: build for me a mosque. ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended only the good"⁠﴾ — by its construction, ﴿except⁠﴾ the deed ﴿of good⁠﴾, which is kindness to the Muslims and widening (of their resources) for them. When they had built that mosque, they asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to come to them and lead them in prayer in that mosque, so Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade him and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 108:

﴿Do not ever stand in it. A mosque founded upon piety⁠—﴾ its walls were built and its foundations raised upon obedience to Allah the Exalted. ﴿From the first day⁠—﴾ it was built and its construction took place; it is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was also said: it is the Mosque of Quba. ﴿Is more worthy that you stand in it⁠—﴾ for prayer. ﴿In it are men⁠—﴾ meaning: the Ansar. ﴿Who love to purify themselves⁠—﴾ meaning: washing the posteriors with water, for it was among their custom in istinja' (cleansing after relieving oneself) to use water after the stone. ﴿And Allah loves those who purify themselves⁠—﴾ from shirk and hypocrisy.

Al-Wahidi, al-Wajiz, commentary on Surah 9, verse 109:

﴿Is one who founded his building﴾ — that is, his structure which he built — ﴿upon piety from God﴾ — fear of God, hope for His reward, and seeking His good pleasure — ﴿better, or one who founded his building upon the brink of a crumbling cliff﴾ — on the edge of a precipice — ﴿so that it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾ — He caused his building to fall ﴿into the fire of Hell﴾. This is a parable, and the meaning is: the building of this mosque is like a building on the brink of Hell, which hurls its builders into it, because it is an act of disobedience and a deed of what God has disliked, namely harm (ḍirār).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 110:

﴿Their building which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾: doubt in their hearts. ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾: by death. The meaning: they will remain in doubt about it until death, thinking that they were doing good in its construction. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He has ordained for each one.

The verse is about the Pledge of al-ʿAqabah (bayʿat al-ʿAqabah), when the Anṣār pledged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would worship Allah and not associate anything with Him, and that they would protect him from what they protect themselves from. They said: "If we do that, O Messenger of Allah, what will we have?" He said: "Paradise." They said: "The sale is profitable; we will not cancel it nor ask for its cancellation." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾ ...

The meaning of ﴿He has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, in return for that they will have Paradise﴾ is that when the believer fights in the way of Allah until he is killed, and spends his wealth in the way of Allah, he receives from Paradise, in the Hereafter, a reward for what he did. His saying ﴿as a promise﴾ means: Allah promised them Paradise as a promise ﴿binding upon Him in truth﴾, with no breaking of it. ﴿In the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an﴾ means: Allah made clear in the two scriptures that He had purchased from the nation of Muḥammad their lives and their properties in return for Paradise, just as He made it clear in the Qur'an. ﴿And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah?﴾ means: no one is more faithful in what he promises than Allah. Then He praised them, saying:

﴿The repentant﴾, i.e., they are those who repent from shirk (associating partners with God). ﴿The worshippers﴾, who hold the worship of God to be obligatory upon them. ﴿The praisers﴾ of God in every state. ﴿The wanderers﴾, i.e., the fasting ones. ﴿Those who bow and prostrate﴾ in the obligatory prayers. ﴿Those who enjoin what is right﴾ by (calling to) faith in God, His obligations, and His limits. And ﴿those who forbid what is wrong﴾, i.e., shirk and the abandoning of God's obligations. ﴿And those who guard the limits of God﴾, i.e., those who act upon what God has made obligatory for them.

The verse is 9:113. Translating the passage:

﴿It is not for the Prophet﴾ and so on. The verse was revealed concerning the Prophet's (peace be upon him) seeking forgiveness for his uncle Abu Talib, and for his father and mother, and the Muslims seeking forgiveness for their polytheist parents. They were forbidden from this. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said: "I will surely seek forgiveness for my father just as Ibrahim sought forgiveness for his father." So Allah, glorified is He, explained how that was, and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 114:

﴿And the seeking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him.﴾ This was because he had promised him that he would ask forgiveness for him, hoping for his conversion to Islam, and that Allah would, through his seeking forgiveness for him, move him from disbelief to Islam. This is evident in His saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord﴾ and His saying: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾. When his father died as a polytheist, he disassociated himself from him and ceased seeking forgiveness. ﴿Indeed, Abraham was ʾawwah (one who sighs much in supplication), ḥalīm (forbearing)﴾, meaning a frequent supplicant who weeps much. ﴿Ḥalīm﴾ means he did not punish anyone except for the sake of Allah, and did not take revenge on anyone except for Allah. When He forbade seeking forgiveness for the polytheists, He made clear that He would not seize them for what they had done, because He had not yet made clear to them that such [seeking of forgiveness] was impermissible. So He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 115:

﴿And Allah would never misguide a people after He had guided them﴾ — that is, He would not place misguidance in their hearts after guidance, ﴿until He makes clear to them what they should avoid﴾ — so that they do not fear Him. At that point they deserve to be led astray.

Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet (ﷺ) for his permitting the hypocrites to stay behind from him, which is what was mentioned in His words: ﴿Allah pardon you﴾, the verse. ﴿And the Muhajirun and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, at the time of the hardship of mounts, the hardship of water, and the hardship of provisions. ﴿After the hearts of a faction of them had nearly deviated﴾, after some of them had resolved to stay behind from him and to disobey, then they caught up with him. ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning His pleasure with them increased.

And (He also turned in mercy) to the three who were left behind, that is, concerning their repentance, meaning those we mentioned in His words: ﴿And others are deferred until Allah's command﴾. ﴿Until, when the earth grew narrow for them despite its vastness﴾, because they were shunned, not dealt with and not spoken to. ﴿And their souls became straitened for them﴾ by the anxiety that had settled within them. ﴿They thought﴾, that is, they became certain, ﴿that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾, that there is no protection from the punishment of Allah except by Him. ﴿Then He turned to them in mercy that they might repent﴾, that is, He showed kindness to them in repentance and granted them success in it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 119:

﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: the People of the Book. ﴿Fear Allah﴾ by obeying Him. ﴿And be with the truthful ones﴾, Muhammad and his companions. He commands them to be with them in jihad, in hardship and in ease.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 120:

And His saying: ﴿Nor should they prefer themselves over His Messenger﴾ — i.e., they should not be content for themselves with ease and comfort while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is in heat and hardship. ﴿That﴾ — i.e., that prohibition against staying behind — ﴿is because they will not suffer thirst﴾, which is intense thirst, ﴿nor fatigue﴾, which is exhaustion from toil, ﴿nor hunger﴾, which is famine, ﴿nor do they tread any path﴾, i.e., they do not take any position ﴿that enrages the disbelievers﴾, that angers them, ﴿nor do they inflict on an enemy any injury﴾, by way of capture or killing, except that it is recorded for them as a good deed ﴿with Allah﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 121:

﴿And they spend no expenditure, small or great﴾ — a date or more than that. ﴿Nor do they cross a valley﴾ — they pass it in their journey. ﴿except that it is recorded for them﴾ — their traces and their steps, ﴿so that Allah may reward them with the best﴾ — with the best ﴿of what they used to do﴾.

When those who stayed behind from the expedition to Tabuk were reproached, the Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not stay behind from any expedition after this, nor from any detachment, ever." So when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the detachments (sara'ya) against the enemy, the Muslims all went forth to the raid and left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alone in Madinah. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 122:

﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all together.﴾ That is, to go forth all together to the ghazw (military campaign). ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth?﴾ That is, why should not a group from every tribe go forth to the ghazw? ﴿That they may gain understanding in the religion,﴾ that they may learn the Qur'an, the sunan (prophetic traditions and practices), and the hudud (legal limits). It means: the division that remains behind. ﴿And that they may warn their people when they return to them,﴾ and teach them what has been revealed of the Qur'an and warn them with it. ﴿That they may be cautious.﴾ So that they do not act contrary to the Qur'an.

O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you [of the disbelievers] (﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا الذين يلونكم﴾). "Those who are near you" means they are close to you. They were commanded to fight the nearest of their enemies, then the next nearest, starting from Medina (﴿يلونكم﴾ / "those who are adjacent to you"). ﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾ — meaning severity and roughness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 124:

﴿And when a surah is revealed, among them﴾ [i.e., among the hypocrites] ﴿is one who says, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ The hypocrites say this to one another in mockery. Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith﴾ [meaning: in affirmation (taṣdīq), because they affirmed the first and the second surah] ﴿and they rejoice﴾ [i.e., they are glad at the revelation of the surah].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 125:

﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ — doubt and hypocrisy — ﴿it adds to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾ — disbelief upon their disbelief, because whenever a surah was revealed and they disbelieved in it, their disbelief increased.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 126:

﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾ They are tried with illnesses and pains, and these are the forerunners of death. ﴿Yet they do not repent﴾ from hypocrisy, and they do not take heed, as the believer takes heed through sickness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 127:

﴿And when a surah is revealed﴾ — when a surah was revealed containing the faults of the hypocrites, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to them, that was difficult for them, and ﴿they glance at one another﴾, wanting to flee from the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some of them said to others: ﴿"Does anyone see you?"﴾ — if you stand up. If no one sees them, they leave the mosque; but if they know that someone sees them, they remain in their places until he finishes his sermon. ﴿Then they turn away﴾ — upon the resolve of disbelief and denial. ﴿Allah has turned their hearts﴾ away from every guidance and right direction ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾ — as a recompense for their deeds, which is that they do not understand from Allah His religion and what Allah called them to.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 9, verse 128:

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, from the Arabs, from the children of Isma'il, so that they may understand him. ﴿It grieves him that you suffer﴾, meaning: your hardship and every harm that befalls you are difficult for him. ﴿He is anxious for you﴾, that you believe. This is addressed to the disbelievers and to whoever has not believed in him. Then he mentions that he is ﴿to the believers, kind and merciful﴾.

﴿Then if they turn away﴾, meaning they turn away from faith: the polytheists and the hypocrites. ﴿Say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."﴾ That is, Allah is the One who suffices me; ﴿there is no god but Him﴾; ﴿in Him I have put my trust﴾, and in Him I have placed my confidence. ﴿And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾; the Throne was singled out for mention because it is the greatest of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has created.
